library.title: 2-Minute Regulation Reset
library.shortSummary: A tiny intervention to stop escalation and regain choice.
library.rationale: Under stress, your body often reacts before your mind. This practice creates a small gap between trigger and response — the gap where autonomy lives. It is intentionally short so it works in real life: before a message, during conflict, or when urgency takes over.
steps: Name the moment in one phrase: “This is the trigger.”
Exhale longer than you inhale for 6–8 breaths.
Relax jaw and shoulders; feel your feet on the ground.
Choose one response: a boundary, a question, or a short break.
reflectionAfter: What changed in my body after two minutes?
Which response did I choose that I would not have chosen on autopilot?

library.title: Clean Request (One Sentence)
library.shortSummary: Replace hints and pressure with a clear, respectful ask.
library.rationale: Many conflicts escalate because needs are communicated indirectly. This practice supports relatedness without sacrificing autonomy. It also increases competence: people can respond to what is actually being asked.
steps: Name what you need (not what they did wrong).
Make one specific request that can receive a yes/no.
Add one sentence of context (why it matters).
Pause and let the other person respond without arguing.
reflectionAfter: Did I ask for a need, or for a story in my head to be fixed?
What happened when I stopped overexplaining?
